open_obligations: Resolve paper Definition 6.1’s literal strict comparison, including self and zero-distance cases, and its query-oracle/input domains. For a selected source-pinned paper machine, construct its query-oracle representation and exact output law, then prove the required universal Lean premise directly or establish an applicable restricted-family theorem. The earlier output-and-distance coverage contract is sufficient but fails for the checked adaptive two-query model even though a separate direct universal proof succeeds at one base.

Independently review and justify the source-shaped Figure 1 Round candidate, including cross-examination, claim/contribution domains, post-bit Bob information, continuous two-party coin to Bernoulli law, conditional verifier samples, sample-count/acceptance constants, and terminal indexing. The checked round_eq_pinned_step theorem applies only to a bit-invisible Bob with reachable coin law and exact claim/decision/verifier component matches; full arbitrary-opponent and resource claims remain open.

Map paper language, machine, inputs, time and resource quantifiers to formal objects; prove any claimed full-thm correctness and complexity consequences from pinned Lean results or keep the narrower correspondence separate.

Obtain source-level review of the remaining Figure 1 body, Protocol.lean, Cost.lean and relevant earlier paper sections before claiming a scoped semantic match; the completed Hatem source check covered only the listed Section 6 extract, Correct.lean and Oracle.lean.
in.rationale: The full paper Theorem 6.2 to pinned Lean correctness relation remains OPEN after an attributed AI-assisted source review. Checked restricted probes expose the query-oracle versus universal history-kernel premise gap and post-bit Bob information gap. A conditional oracle representation theorem identifies the extra coverage sufficient to lift a weak query bound, and has a checked one-address toy instance, but is not established for a paper machine. Checked one-step results reach actual Comp.step for a bit-invisible post-bit variant, and conditionally for an abstract projected round whose four component laws are assumed equal to Lean's; both concern full state-value laws only. No paper-to-Lean theorem, protocol, resource, or empirical transfer follows. A bounded adaptive two-query machine now has exact output and weak finite-input bounds; its representation fails the earlier sufficient coverage condition while a separate direct proof establishes Lean universal Lipschitzness at one specific base. These scoped findings do not settle the paper machine, strict definition, or full theorem. A new source-shaped Figure 1 round has a checked conditional one-step handoff to actual Comp.step, a checked bit-sensitive Bob boundary, and one finite coin-law witness; its separate paper-protocol mapping is only a candidate.

Paper Definition 6.1 is read as Hatem Elshatlawy answered on 2026-10-13: “any other oracle 𝒪′” means an oracle other than 𝒪 itself (answer EXCLUDES_SELF), and the prose “at most”, that is ≤, governs the displayed strict < (answer AT_MOST_GOVERNS). Restated on Lean's oracles at a fixed t and final Boolean event, this reading implies Lean Oracle.lipschitz with the same constant (Lean-checked example at_most_without_self_transfers); the restatement does not map the paper's machine, inputs or supremum over inputs, which stays open as D02.

Settled by a Lean check, not by an answer. How are two different oracles at distance zero treated? In Lean's model, two oracles at distance zero are the same oracle, so there is no such pair and how the paper would treat one cannot change this correctness-only claim (example zero_distance_means_same_oracle; receipt docs/site_product_v1/paper_pilot_v1/review_probe_checks.json, SHA-256 118565f8bee3f8476179e5c49c6d2459dff8df738b83fcc16903b278d69fea8d).
